record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: For every fixed pair of finite graphs X and Y, prove or disprove that there are only finitely many prohibited subgraphs whose absence characterizes finite graphs K that are basically embeddable in X x Y. Basic embeddability is the product-space version of decomposing every continuous real-valued function on K as a sum of functions of the two coordinates.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X and Y be finite (topological) graphs, regarded as one-dimensional compact metric spaces. A finite graph K (viewed as a compact metric space) is said to be basically embeddable in the product X × Y if there exists an embedding e: K → X × Y such that for every continuous function f: K → ℝ there exist continuous functions g: X → ℝ and h: Y → ℝ with f(p) = g(π_X(e(p))) + h(π_Y(e(p))) for all p ∈ K, where π_X and π_Y are the coordinate projections.

A finite graph H is called a prohibited (obstruction) subgraph for basic embeddability in X × Y if H is not basically embeddable in X × Y but every proper subgraph of H is basically embeddable in X × Y (equivalently, the class of finite graphs basically embeddable in X × Y is characterized by the absence of subgraphs from some family, and H is a minimal forbidden member of this family).

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every fixed pair of finite graphs X and Y, there exist only finitely many prohibited subgraphs (up to isomorphism) characterizing the finite graphs K that are basically embeddable in X × Y.
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found that resolves this finiteness question for obstruction sets of basic embeddability into a product X × Y of arbitrary finite graphs. Related work (Skopenkov and others) describes basic embeddability into the plane and characterizes basic embeddability in some specific products, but a general finiteness theorem for prohibited subgraphs in X × Y does not appear to have been established or refuted in the available literature. Status is therefore taken to be unknown.

status_evidence.title: Basic embeddings and Hilbert's 13th problem on superpositions
status_evidence.snippet: The notion of a basic embedding appeared in the course of the Kolmogorov-Arnold solution of Hilbert's 13th problem on superpositions. Descriptions of basic subsets of the plane and graphs basically embeddable into the plane are presented.
status_evidence.claim: Survey of basic embeddability results does not establish a general finite-obstruction theorem for arbitrary products X × Y of finite graphs.

status_evidence.title: Invariants of Graph Drawings in the Plane (Skopenkov)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses embeddability invariants for graphs but does not provide a general finiteness statement for prohibited subgraphs of basic embeddability in products of finite graphs.
status_evidence.claim: No general resolution of the finite-obstruction problem for basic embeddability in X × Y is given.
